season.evidence: Stored season blank. Ascent histogram: Jun 30, Jul 54, Aug 29, Sep 47, Oct 28 successful logs; snow lingers on trail and in the basin into June. Web (Wenatchee Outdoors West Route page, Mountaineers Emerald and Saska page, Summitpost) names no season but suggests midsummer and fall larch; so core Jul-Sep, with Jun and Oct as the one-month shoulders.

Jul 5 2026, start 112 m from our trailhead pin, one-way, no logged route or report text; cannot say which line.

facts.text: In mid-June the North Fork Entiat trail had many fallen trees, the first three to four miles run through burned forest with little shade, and snow patches covered the trail from about 6,600 to 6,900 ft.
By early July the trail had been cleared of most blowdowns, though a few logs still needed climbing over, and the basin below the peak had plenty of water and no snow crossings.
Flat tent sites with running water sit in the larch basin between Emerald and Saska at roughly 6,800-6,900 ft, which makes a good base from June through September.
In mid-June the basin below the peak still holds snow (soft by mid-morning) and the west gully is filled with steep snow around 8,150 ft.

notes: Two routes on the peak (SE Ridge already has a track). Every harvested track follows the standard talus/south-west slopes or an unnamed line; none positively names our west gully, so no track is assigned. The only clear west-gully report took a different upper line because of snow. Our trailhead pin (48.01076,-120.57224) is confirmed by the many tracks starting within ~50 m of it, but no pin change is needed.
